parts.solutionMd:
> *Use the binomial expansion formula*

$\left(a + b\right)^{n} = a^{n} + \begin{bmatrix} n \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} a^{n - 1} b + \begin{bmatrix} n \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} a^{n - 2} b^{2} . . . + \begin{bmatrix} n \\ r \end{bmatrix} a^{n - r} b^{r} + . . . + b^{n}$

> *Substitute *$a=5$*, *$b = \left(2 x\right)$* and *$n=5$* into the first three terms of the formula*

$\left(5 + 2 x\right)^{5} = 5^{5} + \begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} 5^{5 - 1} \left(2 x\right) + \begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} 5^{5 - 2} \left(2 x\right)^{2} + . . .$

> *Find the binomial coefficients e.g. using the *${}_{}^{n}{C_{r}}$* button on your calculator or Pascal's triangle*

$\left(\begin{pmatrix}5 \\ 1\end{pmatrix}\right) = 5$
$\left(\begin{pmatrix}5 \\ 2\end{pmatrix}\right) = 10$

**[M1]**

> *Substitute these into the formula and simplify*

> *Remember to use index laws, e.g. *$\left(2 x\right)^{2} = 2^{2} x^{2} = 4 x^{2}$

$\begin{aligned}\left(5 + 2 x\right)^{5} & = & 5^{5} + 5 \times 5^{4} \left(2 x\right) + 10 \times 5^{3} \left(2 x\right)^{2} + . . . \\ & = & 5^{5} + 5 \times 5^{4} \times 2 x + 10 \times 5^{3} \times 4 x^{2} + . . .\end{aligned}$

$3125+6250x+5000x^{2}$

**[M1 A1]**
